items.stem: You took a $12 taxi ride for work. Do you need a receipt to claim it?
items.stem_ar: ركبت تاكسي للشغل بـ 12 دولار. محتاج إيصال عشان تطلب المبلغ؟

options.text: Yes, every expense needs a receipt
options.text_ar: أيوه، أي مصروف لازم له إيصال
options.feedback: Not quite: receipts are required only for expenses over $25.
Right. The policy requires a receipt for every expense over $25.

options.text: Only if your manager asks for it
options.feedback: The rule is a fixed $25 threshold, not the manager's choice.

items.explanation: Receipts are required for every expense over $25 (Expense Policy §4.1).

items.stem: A claim submitted 100 days after the expense will still be reimbursed.

options.feedback: No: claims older than 90 days are not reimbursed.
Correct: after 90 days claims are not reimbursed.

items.stem: Put the claim steps in order.

options.text: Open Northwind Expenses and select New Claim
Enter category, date, amount and purpose

items.scenario: Your hotel bill is $260 for one night. Your colleague suggests splitting it into two claims of $130.

options.feedback: Splitting one expense to stay under a limit is never allowed.

options.text: Submit one claim and ask the Travel Desk about the cap
options.feedback: Yes: one expense, one claim; the Travel Desk can approve an exception to the $220 cap.

options.text: Pay the difference yourself and claim $220 twice
options.feedback: That is still splitting and inflating the claim.

items.explanation: Never split one expense into several claims to stay under an approval limit; hotel costs above $220 per night need a Travel Desk exception.

items.back: A fixed daily allowance for meals and incidentals on overnight business travel.
